title: Sex-linked polygenic architecture in advertisement signals and mate preferences, and ecological compatibility, in two members of the Enchenopa binotata complex of treehoppers (Hemiptera: Membracidae)
content:
Abstract
We used a hybridization experiment to explore the genetic architecture of ecological adaptation and advertisement signals and mate preferences in two members of the Enchenopa binotata species complex of treehoppers, a clade of plant-feeding insects that offers a case study of speciation involving ecological and sexual selection. We found evidence of ecological compatibility (comparable survival to the adult stage on the same host plant in the parental species and the hybrids); and evidence for sex-linked polygenic architecture of male signals and female mate preferences. These results have intriguing implications for the course of speciation: selection to avoid maladaptive hybridization might not be crucial; the establishment of signal–preference linkage disequilibrium might often be facilitated by trait genetic architecture; and sexual divergence might suffice to keep species distinct.
